beats.text: In 1933, an airliner exploded in the night sky outside Chesterton, Indiana. It was a bomb. No one has ever learned who planted it.
beats.label: NEAR CHESTERTON, INDIANA

beats.text: October 10, 1933. A United Air Lines Boeing 247, bound for California, was flying from Cleveland to Chicago.
beats.label: OCTOBER 10, 1933

beats.text: Around 9 that night, people on the ground heard an explosion. Witnesses said the burning plane was about 1,000 feet up.
beats.label: AROUND 9 P.M.

beats.text: It came down in Jackson Township, outside Chesterton. All seven people aboard were lost.
beats.label: JACKSON TOWNSHIP

beats.text: Federal agents found that a bomb had gone off in the rear of the plane, probably nitroglycerin.
beats.label: THE INVESTIGATION

beats.text: It is the first proven bombing of a commercial airliner. The case was closed in 1935, and never solved.
beats.label: CASE CLOSED, 1935
